metadata.title: Greedy Function Approximation: A Gradient Boosting Machine
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced (some equations garbled in PDF text-layer; reconstructed by best-effort using context).

nodes.name: Function Estimation Problem
nodes.statement: Find $F^*(x) = \arg\min_{F(x)} E_{y,x}\, \Psi(y, F(x))$ given training sample $\{y_i, x_i\}_1^N$, where $\Psi$ is a specified loss function.
nodes.statement_clean: Estimate the function mapping inputs x to output y that minimizes expected loss over the joint distribution.

nodes.name: Additive Expansion
nodes.statement: Parameterized class of functions $F(x; P) = \sum_{m=0}^{M} \beta_m h(x; a_m)$ where $P = \{\beta_m, a_m\}_0^M$ and $h(x; a)$ are simple base functions of $x$.

nodes.name: Common Loss Functions
nodes.statement: Squared-error $\Psi(y, F) = (y - F)^2$ and absolute error $\Psi(y, F) = |y - F|$ for regression ($y \in \mathbb{R}$); negative binomial log-likelihood $\Psi(y, F) = \log(1 + e^{-2yF})$ for classification ($y \in \{-1, 1\}$).

nodes.name: Steepest-Descent Increments
nodes.statement: Increments $p_m = -\rho_m g_m$ where $g_m = [\partial \Phi(P)/\partial P_j]_{P=P_{m-1}}$ is the current gradient and $\rho_m = \arg\min_\rho \Phi(P_{m-1} - \rho g_m)$ is the line search step length.

nodes.name: Function-Space Steepest-Descent
nodes.statement: In function space, the increment is $f_m(x) = -\rho_m g_m(x)$ with $g_m(x) = E_y\left[\partial \Psi(y, F(x))/\partial F(x) \mid x\right]_{F(x)=F_{m-1}(x)}$ and $\rho_m = \arg\min_\rho E_{y,x}\, \Psi(y, F_{m-1}(x) - \rho g_m(x))$.

nodes.name: Greedy-Stagewise Approach
nodes.statement: For $m = 1, \ldots, M$: solve $(\beta_m, a_m) = \arg\min_{\beta, a} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \Psi(y_i, F_{m-1}(x_i) + \beta h(x_i, a))$, then set $F_m(x) = F_{m-1}(x) + \beta_m h(x, a_m)$.

nodes.name: Constrained Negative Gradient
nodes.statement: The base learner $h(x, a_m)$ most parallel to the unconstrained negative gradient $\{-g_m(x_i)\}_1^N$ is $a_m = \arg\min_{a, \beta} \sum_{i=1}^{N} [-g_m(x_i) - \beta h(x_i, a)]^2$.

nodes.name: Gradient Boost
nodes.statement: Generic gradient-descent boosting algorithm that fits a base learner to pseudo-responses (negative gradients of the loss) and updates via line search.
nodes.pseudocode: 1. $F_0(x) = \arg\min_\rho \sum_{i=1}^N \Psi(y_i, \rho)$. 2. For $m = 1$ to $M$: 3. $\tilde{y}_i = -[\partial \Psi(y_i, F(x_i))/\partial F(x_i)]_{F(x)=F_{m-1}(x)}$, $i = 1, \ldots, N$. 4. $a_m = \arg\min_{a, \beta} \sum_{i=1}^N [\tilde{y}_i - \beta h(x_i, a)]^2$. 5. $\rho_m = \arg\min_\rho \sum_{i=1}^N \Psi(y_i, F_{m-1}(x_i) + \rho h(x_i, a_m))$. 6. $F_m(x) = F_{m-1}(x) + \rho_m h(x, a_m)$. 7. endFor.

nodes.name: LS Boost
nodes.statement: Gradient boosting with squared-error loss $\Psi(y, F) = (y - F)^2/2$, which iteratively fits the current residuals.
nodes.pseudocode: $F_0(x) = \bar{y}$. For $m = 1$ to $M$: $\tilde{y}_i = y_i - F_{m-1}(x_i)$, $(\rho_m, a_m) = \arg\min_{a, \beta} \sum_{i=1}^N [\tilde{y}_i - \beta h(x_i, a)]^2$, $F_m(x) = F_{m-1}(x) + \rho_m h(x, a_m)$.

nodes.name: LAD TreeBoost
nodes.statement: Gradient boosting for least-absolute-deviation regression $\Psi(y, F) = |y - F|$ with $L$-terminal-node trees, using the sign of residuals as pseudo-response and median updates per terminal node.
nodes.pseudocode: $F_0(x) = \mathrm{median}\{y_i\}_1^N$. For $m = 1$ to $M$: $\tilde{y}_i = \mathrm{sign}(y_i - F_{m-1}(x_i))$; $\{R_{lm}\}_1^L = L$-terminal-node-tree($\{\tilde{y}_i, x_i\}_1^N$); $\gamma_{lm} = \mathrm{median}_{x_i \in R_{lm}}\{y_i - F_{m-1}(x_i)\}$; $F_m(x) = F_{m-1}(x) + \gamma_{lm} \mathbf{1}(x \in R_{lm})$.

nodes.name: M TreeBoost
nodes.statement: Gradient boosting with Huber M loss for robust regression, using $L$-terminal-node trees with a Newton-like single-step update around the per-node median of residuals.
nodes.pseudocode: $F_0(x) = \mathrm{median}\{y_i\}_1^N$. For $m = 1$ to $M$: $r_{m-1}(x_i) = y_i - F_{m-1}(x_i)$; $\delta_m = \mathrm{quantile}_\alpha\{|r_{m-1}(x_i)|\}$; $\tilde{y}_i = r_{m-1}(x_i)$ if $|r_{m-1}(x_i)| \le \delta_m$ else $\delta_m \cdot \mathrm{sign}(r_{m-1}(x_i))$; build $L$-terminal-node tree on $\{\tilde{y}_i, x_i\}$ with regions $\{R_{lm}\}$; $\tilde{r}_{lm} = \mathrm{median}_{x_i \in R_{lm}}\{r_{m-1}(x_i)\}$; $\gamma_{lm} = \tilde{r}_{lm} + \frac{1}{N_{lm}}\sum_{x_i \in R_{lm}} \mathrm{sign}(r_{m-1}(x_i) - \tilde{r}_{lm}) \cdot \min(\delta_m, |r_{m-1}(x_i) - \tilde{r}_{lm}|)$; $F_m(x) = F_{m-1}(x) + \gamma_{lm} \mathbf{1}(x \in R_{lm})$.

nodes.name: L2 TreeBoost
nodes.statement: Gradient boosting for two-class logistic regression with negative binomial log-likelihood, using $L$-terminal-node trees and a single Newton-Raphson step for terminal-node updates.
output: Log-odds approximation $F_M(x)$ from which probabilities $p_+(x) = 1/(1 + e^{-2 F_M(x)})$ are derived
nodes.pseudocode: $F_0(x) = \frac{1}{2} \log\frac{1+\bar{y}}{1-\bar{y}}$. For $m = 1$ to $M$: $\tilde{y}_i = 2 y_i / (1 + \exp(2 y_i F_{m-1}(x_i)))$; $\{R_{lm}\}_1^L = L$-terminal-node-tree($\{\tilde{y}_i, x_i\}$); $\gamma_{lm} = \sum_{x_i \in R_{lm}} \tilde{y}_i / \sum_{x_i \in R_{lm}} |\tilde{y}_i|(2 - |\tilde{y}_i|)$; $F_m(x) = F_{m-1}(x) + \gamma_{lm} \mathbf{1}(x \in R_{lm})$.

nodes.name: LK TreeBoost
nodes.statement: Gradient boosting for $K$-class logistic regression using the symmetric multinomial logit; induces $K$ trees per iteration with diagonal-Hessian Newton-Raphson terminal updates.
nodes.pseudocode: $F_{k0}(x) = 0$, $k = 1, \ldots, K$. For $m = 1$ to $M$: compute $p_k(x) = \exp(F_k(x)) / \sum_l \exp(F_l(x))$; for $k = 1$ to $K$: $\tilde{y}_{ik} = y_{ik} - p_k(x_i)$; build $L$-terminal-node tree with regions $\{R_{klm}\}$; $\gamma_{klm} = \frac{K-1}{K} \cdot \sum_{x_i \in R_{klm}} \tilde{y}_{ik} / \sum_{x_i \in R_{klm}} |\tilde{y}_{ik}|(1 - |\tilde{y}_{ik}|)$; $F_{km}(x) = F_{k,m-1}(x) + \gamma_{klm} \mathbf{1}(x \in R_{klm})$.

nodes.name: Influence Trimming
nodes.statement: Delete observations whose weight $w_i$ falls below $w_{l(\alpha)}$, where $l(\alpha)$ solves $\sum_{i=1}^{l(\alpha)} w_{(i)} = \alpha \sum_{i=1}^N w_i$ and $w_i = \exp(-2 y_i F_{m-1}(x_i))$ or $w_i = |\tilde{y}_i|(2 - |\tilde{y}_i|)$. Typical $\alpha \in [0.05, 0.2]$.

nodes.name: Proportional Shrinkage Regularization
nodes.statement:
Replace the update step $F_m(x) = F_{m-1}(x) + ho_m h(x, a_m)$ with $F_m(x) = F_{m-1}(x) + 
u \cdot ho_m h(x, a_m)$, $0 < 
u \le 1$, where $
u$ is a learning-rate / shrinkage parameter.

nodes.name: ANOVA Functional Decomposition
nodes.statement: $F(x) = \sum_j f_j(x_j) + \sum_{j,k} f_{jk}(x_j, x_k) + \sum_{j,k,l} f_{jkl}(x_j, x_k, x_l) + \cdots$, where the first sum is the additive (main-effects) component and successive sums capture interaction effects of increasing order.

nodes.name: Tree-Size Controls Interaction Order
nodes.statement: An $L$-terminal-node tree produces a function with interaction order at most $\min(L-1, n)$. Consequently the interaction order of a TreeBoost approximation is bounded by that of its individual trees.
assumptions: Best-first decision trees with $L$ terminal nodes

nodes.name: Relative Influence (continuous)
nodes.statement: For a continuous approximation, $J_j = \left(E_x\left[\partial \hat{F}(x)/\partial x_j\right]^2 \mathrm{var}_x[x_j]\right)^{1/2}$ measures the influence of input $x_j$ on the variation of $\hat{F}$.

nodes.name: Tree-Based Relative Influence
nodes.statement: For a single tree $T$: $\hat{J}_j^2(T) = \sum_{t=1}^{L-1} \hat{I}_t^2 \mathbf{1}(v_t = j)$ summed over non-terminal nodes, where $v_t$ is the splitting variable and $\hat{I}_t^2$ is the squared-error improvement from the split. For a boosted ensemble $\{T_m\}_1^M$: $\hat{J}_j^2 = \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m=1}^M \hat{J}_j^2(T_m)$.
nodes.origin_citation: Breiman, Friedman, Olshen, Stone 1983 (extended to ensembles here)

nodes.name: Least-Squares Split Improvement
nodes.statement: $I^2(R_l, R_r) = \frac{w_l w_r}{w_l + w_r} (\bar{y}_l - \bar{y}_r)^2$, where $\bar{y}_l, \bar{y}_r$ are the daughter response means and $w_l, w_r$ the corresponding weight sums.

nodes.name: Linear-Target Justification of Tree Influence
nodes.statement: If $F^*(x) = a_0 + \sum_j a_j x_j$ and the input covariance is a multiple of the identity $E_x[(x - \bar{x})(x - \bar{x})^T] = c I_n$, then the continuous relative-influence measure satisfies $J_j = |a_j|$.

nodes.name: Partial Dependence Function
nodes.statement: For input subset $z_l \subset x$ with complement $z_{\setminus l}$: $\bar{F}_l(z_l) = E_{z_{\setminus l}}[\hat{F}(x)] = \int \hat{F}(x)\, p_{\setminus l}(z_{\setminus l})\, d z_{\setminus l}$, the marginal-density average summarizing the dependence of $\hat{F}$ on $z_l$.

nodes.name: Marginal vs Conditional Averaging
nodes.statement: Averaging over the conditional density $p(z_{\setminus l} \mid z_l)$ gives $\tilde{F}_l(z_l) = E_x[\hat{F}(x) \mid z_l]$, which conflates the dependence of $\hat{F}$ on $z_l$ with associations to $z_{\setminus l}$; the marginal-density form (46) is preferred unless inputs are independent.

nodes.name: Weighted Tree-Traversal for Partial Dependence
nodes.statement: Compute $\bar{F}_l(z_l)$ on a decision tree by a weighted root-to-leaf traversal: at $z_l$-splits follow the appropriate child; at $z_{\setminus l}$-splits visit both children with weights proportional to the training fraction going each way. Aggregate over the $M$ trees of a boosted ensemble.

nodes.name: Shrinkage-vs-Iterations Simulation
nodes.statement: Simulation with 5000 observations, normal noise (SNR 2:1), 11-terminal-node trees, and shrinkage $\nu \in \{1.0, 0.25, 0.125, 0.06\}$ shows that smaller $\nu$ requires larger optimal $M$ but yields lower lack-of-fit; the misclassification error-rate is much less sensitive to over-fitting than the negative log-likelihood.

nodes.name: Random Function Generator
nodes.statement: Targets $F^*(x) = \sum_{l=1}^{20} a_l g_l(z_l)$ with $a_l \sim U[-1, 1]$ and $g_l(z_l) = \exp(-\frac{1}{2}(z_l - \mu_l)^T V_l (z_l - \mu_l))$ are randomly generated; $z_l$ is a random size-$n_l$ subset of $x$ with $n_l = \lfloor 1.5 + r \rfloor$, $r \sim \mathrm{Exp}(2)$. 100 such target functions are used in the simulation studies.

nodes.name: Error-Distribution Comparison: LS vs LAD vs M TreeBoost
nodes.statement: Over 100 random targets with 1:1 SNR: under normal errors LS TreeBoost wins 73 trials and is on average 0.2% worse than the best while LAD is 7.4% worse; under slash errors LS is disastrous (364.6% worse on average) while M TreeBoost is best 68 times and 1.0% worse on average. M TreeBoost is the overall method of choice.

nodes.name: LS TreeBoost vs MARS
nodes.statement: On the 100 randomly generated targets with normal errors and 1:1 SNR, MARS and LS TreeBoost have similar average-absolute error, but MARS root-mean-squared error is typically 30% larger, indicating MARS predictions are either very close or very far from the target while LS TreeBoost errors are more uniform.

nodes.name: LK TreeBoost vs LogitBoost vs AdaBoost.MH (5-class)
nodes.statement: Over 100 5-class targets ($N=7500$, 11-terminal-node trees), LK TreeBoost wins 78 trials and is 0.6% worse than the best on average; LogitBoost wins 21 and is 3.5% worse; AdaBoost.MH never wins and is 15% worse. With proportional shrinkage ($\nu = 0.1$) added to LogitBoost and AdaBoost.MH, all three perform similarly.

nodes.name: Tree-Size Effect Simulation
nodes.statement: On the 100 random targets, $L \in \{2, 3, 6, 11, 21\}$: smallest trees ($L \le 2$) give wider error distributions; $L \in \{6, 11, 21\}$ are similar with little difference. Mean relative-to-best errors: 23.2%, 16.4%, 2.4%, 2.2%, 3.7%.

nodes.name: Garnet Data
nodes.statement: $N = 13317$ garnets with 11 chemical concentrations and a categorical tectonic-plate variable. Predict TiO$_2$ from the others. Six-terminal-node trees suffice; LAD and M TreeBoost outperform LS, with Ga and Zr the most influential variables and a strong Ga-Zr interaction visible in partial-dependence plots.

nodes.name: Demographic Data
nodes.statement: $N = 9409$ shopping-mall questionnaires with 14 demographic variables. Predict income from the other 13. Differences among LS / LAD / M TreeBoost are small; an additive ($L = 2$) model suffices; no small group of variables dominates relative importance.

nodes.name: Robustness and Invariances of TreeBoost
nodes.statement: All TreeBoost procedures are invariant under (strictly) monotone transformations of individual input variables, immune to long-tailed input distributions, and robust to irrelevant inputs. LAD/M TreeBoost are additionally robust to output outliers.

nodes.name: Computational Scaling
nodes.statement: After sorting, regression TreeBoost (LS, LAD, M) scales linearly in $N$, $n$, $M$ and roughly logarithmically in $L$. LK TreeBoost scales linearly in $K$ but sub-linearly in $M$ when influence trimming is used.
